newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds fall after Fed source comments.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds fall after Fed source comments.

text.p: Hawkish comments from a Federal Reserve official toppled U.S. mortgaged-backed securities late Tuesday morning and held them there throughout the day, traders said.

In an interview with Reuters, the official said many U.S. central bankers believe the federal funds rate will be raised at least 25 basis points at the Fed's policy meeting next Tuesday, September 24.
Pass-throughs slipped about half a point in most coupons during the half hour of trading after the story, and they stayed near that level into late Tuesday afternoon.
Late on Tuesday, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent coupons were off 11/32 at 100-16/32, yielding 118 basis points over 10-year Treasuries.
Comparable Fannie Mae certificates had dipped 14/32 to 100-14/32, and Freddie Macs had fallen 14/32 to 100-17/32.
Government securities continued their slide late in the day, as technicals-driven trades furthered their losses, fixed-income analysts said.
